title: Abyssal Lapidary is making the social media rounds and I can confirm cutting gemstones is just as satisfying as it looks
summary: I'm a chump who can't tell my gems from my minerals.
body: I have never really thought much about gemstones or minerals, which is weird considering one of my all-time favourite games is Minecraft, in which I spend a bulk of my time strip-mining. But Abyssal Lapidary has made me realise that there is so much more to the dirt than just coal. In the demo for Abyssal Lapidary I got to begin my stint as a lapidarist, someone who cuts, shapes, grinds, and polishes minerals to make pretty gemstones. The only problem is, like I said before, I don't really know stones. (Image credit: LightWorm) Abyssal Lapidary doesn't exactly drop you in the deep end but it does expect you to pick up with the art of making and selling gemstones rather quickly. My first step was searching around the rather large house I'd found myself in which was apparently part of a declining business but it seemed rather nice; it even had a balcony. Most of the doors downstairs were locked, part of the later progression of the game, the few things I did have access to included a station for fixing tools, breaking rocks, and a booth to talk to customers. Throughout the day people will turn up to my humble business either looking to buy some precious gemstones or selling minerals…

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 actually runs pretty smoothly with Activision's 'recommended' RTX 3060 Ti graphics card, and here are the settings I use to get the best performance from it
summary: Though upscaling is somewhat of a requirement if you're at 1440p.
body: I've been having a grand old time playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 with an RX 9070 XT , but there'll be plenty of people wanting to run the game on older hardware. So, I decided to dust off my old and much-beloved workhorse, the RTX 3060 Ti , and see how it does in the new Activision shooter. I've been quite pleasantly surprised by the results. Which is good news, considering Activision lists this graphics card, alongside the AMD RX 6600 XT and Intel Arc B580, as the 'recommended' ones to "run at 90 fps in multiplayer on High graphics settings." I've found this actually pans out, provided you're at 1080p or are fine enabling Quality upscaling at 1440p. title: AMD says the re-release of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D was 'like a final gift to our loyal [AM4] users' and it was CEO Dr. Lisa Su who first came up with the idea
summary: It timed itself rather nicely with the deepening memory crisis, too.
body: I was genuinely surprised by the re-release of the AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D earlier this year. A chip I thought long dead was back in 10th Anniversary form, after a resurrection process AMD's David McAfee described as " very hard, actually " to our Dave at Computex 2026. Now AMD's Travis Kirsch has spoken to Japanese outlet Tech+ about more of the thinking behind the re-release, and it seems the idea started at the very top. "Originally, several years ago, I believe Lisa [Su, AMD CEO] was one of the people who suggested reviving the Ryzen 7 5800X3D." "It was like a final gift to our loyal users who had used our AM4 for almost 10 years, giving them one last chance to upgrade their PCs using DDR4 systems," Kirsch continues. "However, this required restarting the production lines, which took some time. In short, this was planned before the changes in the memory market occurred, and it was not considered as a solution to the DDR5 shortage." That may be the case, but the timing still worked out pretty well for AMD. DDR5 prices had been surging since October 2025, while the chip's eventual release date of June 25, 2026 put it right in the middle of a difficult year for PC gamers. Many of who…

title: AMD says its working on FSR's frame pacing issues, but there's still conspicuously no mention of Multi Frame Generation
summary: Smooth moves ahead?
body: Whether you dismiss it as 'fake frames' or embrace the tech as a real game changer, frame generation has fast become a headlining act of this GPU generation. We've since discovered that not all frame gen (FG) tech is created equal, but AMD has promised to address a key criticism of its own FSR FG. Earlier this week, AMD's Jack Huynh announced that FSR 4.1 would be shipping early to RX 6000 graphics cards , though that wasn't all. Huynh also announced that improvements to FSR's frame pacing were on the way, too . Personally, I'm more familiar with Nvidia's approach to FG—especially after unlocking Multi Frame Gen on my RTX 4070 Super earlier this year. AMD's FSR has often been criticised for how it struggles with frame pacing in comparison. Ie, you may have lots of frames , but not every one of them is displayed for a consistent amount of time, making for gameplay that's a different flavour of choppy. The issue can affect frames both traditionally rendered and generated, and it's been a stumbling block since at least FSR 3. title: In a rare instance of good news, Philips has announced the world's first 36-inch, 260 Hz gaming monitor. So that's nice
summary: Let's all look upon it with wonder.
body: Writing (and reading) about PC hardware news at the moment can be downright depressing. Massive price rises. AI everywhere. Disappearing graphics cards . It's just a bit much, you know? So come and bask in something deliciously old school with me: the release of a good-looking new product you might be able to buy without selling a kidney. Philips says its new 36M4C5500P display is the world's first 36-inch gaming monitor with a 260 Hz refresh rate . Lovely. This ultrawide's got a curved, 1500R VA panel. Oooooh. A 3440 x 1440 resolution. Ahhhh. And an overclockable refresh rate that makes sense for casual and competitive gamers alike. Stone the crows and call the fire department, it actually looks pretty decent. Sure, VA panel tech is nothing fancy. And many a curved ultrawide has passed the doors of PC Gamer Towers over the past few years. But a 36-inch panel size is something interesting, filling the gap between your standard 34-inch ultrawides and the more desk-dominating, 39-inch-and-up models. title: LG UltraGear Evo 52G930B Evo gaming monitor review
summary: LG's new 52-inch ultrawide 5K2K monster monitor is surprisingly old school.
body: Can you have too much of a mediocre thing? If I was being unkind, that's the challenge I'd make to the new LG UltraGear Evo 52G930B . What we are talking about here, people, is a monumental 52-inch 5K2K gaming monitor. But it's based on an old-school VA panel. Yep, not OLED. Not IPS. It doesn't even have mini-LED local dimming. It's just a huge, high-res, VA panel. At 52 inches, it's so big and so expensive it immediately poses another problem. Why wouldn't you just buy a 4K TV? After all, this LG clocks in at $1,699 or £1,499, which buys you an awful lot of 4K TV here in late 2026. That kind of money puts you in reach of OLED TVs up to around 65 inches. And, like I said, the LG UltraGear Evo 52G930B isn't actually that well specced save for its size and resolution. title: I've tested every graphics setting in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4—tweak these four options for the best performance
summary: Upscaling can also help a bunch, of course.
body: I'm not usually one for all these fancy graphics; give me more frames, at all costs. But when I booted up Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , I have to admit, I was a little reluctant to sacrifice too much in the visual department. Because the game is, indeed, gorgeous despite being a little glitchy with texture pop-ins and flickering in DMZ mode. A more tailored approach was needed. So, I set about testing every single graphics setting in the game, one by one, to see which ones have the biggest impact, and I found there are four main settings to tweak. First things first, though, if you just want to get up and going and you're using a mid-range PC, whack it on the Balanced preset, and you'll be fine. If you're using a high-end rig, then you should be fine setting it to the Ultra preset. Note: All performance figures were calculated by doing the same 30-second run in-game, on Mission 4 of the campaign. title: Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 router review
summary: Asus delivers the first Wi-Fi 8 router.
body: We’re not surprised that Asus has delivered the first Wi-Fi 8 router. The company has been ruling the router roost recently and notably broke the 3,000 Mbps transfer-rate barrier with its AI-enhanced, ROG Rapture GT-BE19000AI Wi-Fi 7 gaming router. That’s old hat now that its functionally-identical Wi-Fi 8 sibling, the Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro , is here. Or is it? Wi-Fi 8 (also known as 802.11bn) is expected to be officially ratified in late 2028. By the time you read this, at least four routers will have hit the market, but no laptops (or other devices) are in sight. But, that shouldn’t matter. We've spent some time in the last year testing top-tier Wi-Fi 7 set-ups, and seeing they can be faster than some 10 Gbps wired connections, so why do we need another Wi-Fi generation? However, unlike previous generations, Wi-Fi 8 isn’t about delivering more speed, it’s about delivering a more-reliable signal (including more-robust uploading), to new and old devices alike, in crowded Wi-Fi environments, over greater distances, in real-world environments. title: A public outing of severe and unfixed Linux kernel vulnerabilities should have you thinking of updating your SteamOS or other distros to beta branches
summary: The accidental reveal of unpatched vulnerabilities as high as 9 on the CVSS score chart is a little worrisome.
body: If you're an enlightened sort, who has sought out the sunny uplands of a Linux operating system for your gaming rig in these exciting days of almost seamless game compatibility, then you might want to have a think about migrating your OS onto a beta branch for a while. A list of as-yet unpatched Linux kernel vulnerabilities has been sent out to a public mailing list by accident, and some of these issues score as high as 9 on the CVSS security-scare-o-meter. The incident was reported by Phoronix yesterday, where Michael Larabel noted that overnight several new vulnerability reports had gone to a public rather than private security mailing list. The reports had seemingly come from Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative—an initiative set up to promote extended vulnerability reporting (.pdf warning) with a bug bounty system extending to a group of external researchers. I guess sometimes a group can be too extended. Anyways, the list of vulnerabilities was jumped on by what Phoronix calls Linux's second-in-command, Greg Kroah-Hartman, who maintains the stable branch of the kernel. Kroah-Hartman responded to each of the reports individually asking them to fix their submission process. Mostly…

summary: Stuntboost is a racing game for FPS movement sickos.
body: Fast-paced. 3D Platformer. Parkour. First-Person. Racing. Those are the tags affixed to the Steam page for Stuntboost , a game that I've had trouble summing up with a clean label when asked about it. Stuntboost is a skateboarding game that sometimes features a car, a platformer with a speedometer, an ode to those shrunken bedroom maps popularized by early FPS modders. It's also, quite easily, my favorite game of 2026 so far. Yet, Stuntboost could've easily slipped under my radar. It's been out for a month and hasn't made a big splash on Steam—it's rated "Very Positive" with 253 reviews. I only found it through a friend's recommendation, and even then, the art style didn't immediately suggest it was my thing. title: A new Fallout 4 mod adds an entire town, but more importantly, it lets you join a gang
summary: They're not the Tunnel Snakes, but they're trying.
body: There's nothing I like more in a Fallout game then stumbling across some weird little settlement filled with oddball characters. So when I saw that this mod for Fallout 4 added a whole new town called Detour that's built on top of an overpass near Bedford Station, that was an instant download. Better yet, the mod features new quests and over a dozen new characters voiced by real people—no AI was used! But there's something better than that , even. I was delighted to discover that the town of Detour has its own gang . It's a small gang, sure: the overpass Detour is built on isn't particularly big and the town itself is pretty tiny, so there's not a whole lot of room for different factions to spring up. But that doesn't stop the members of the Detour Degens from occupying one little corner of the town where they hang out in matching jackets, smoking cigs, chugging from beer bottles, and looking tough. Sort of. Look, the Detour Degens are no Tunnel Snakes, that's for sure. But they live on an overpass. They're doing their best. There are a few different types of missions you can do to raise your reputation with the town of Detour, and besides helping out the sheriff with bounties and…

title: How to dual wield in Cyberpunk 2077
summary: Combo your pistols or revolvers with the 2.5 update.
body: (Image credit: CD Projekt) You can now dual wield certain weapons in Cyberpunk 2077 thanks to its Edgerunners 2.5 patch, though sadly it's limited to revolvers and pistols from the power category, which you can either use dual-wielded, or mix and match if you want to have multiple iconics at once. First, though, you need to unlock the Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree at 9. There are also four subsidiary perks, which improve your dual-wielding proficiency. There are a few important things to remember: Dual-wielded iconics will retain their abilities and effects. Dual wielding two weapons will make them weaker, though this is somewhat mitigated via Double Trouble's other perks. title: Future Capcom games will have Onimusha to thank for RE Engine's gnarly dismemberments
summary: Surely this will come in handy for the next Resident Evil.
body: Onimusha: Way of the Sword has received universal praise for its combat animations, which somehow manage to look natural and fluid no matter what angle or direction hero Miyamoto Musashi has to swing his sword to parry an incoming blow. In a post-launch interview, I asked Capcom how—beyond doing a ton of work across Onimusha's lengthy development—they managed to raise the bar for this sort of action game. "Starting the project six years ago, we felt it was important to have that detail to sell the power and the excitement of the action, so it's something we really focused on," said director Satoru Nihei. "Even at that starting point, we knew it was something that Capcom, as a company, have as a great strength: We have a lot of assets and tech available to us that allow us to create these varieties of actions. That's something we really felt we could leverage to make the game really stand out that a lot of other places can't really copy. On top of producing a lot of animations and motion capture, we have to give a lot of credit to the programmers for taking that data and putting it in a form that we can have them make these very smooth transitions, with these physics-based calculat…

title: Splash Damage acquired this studio just 3 months after laying off a bunch of people—now it's laying them off, too
summary: An undisclosed number of employees have been let go from the studio behind survival game Scum.
body: The closure of BioWare and layoff of roughly 400 people at Electronic Arts is being rightly excoriated as an example of the corrosive effects of capital on pretty much everything good. But that same sort of thing happens, maybe more often than we'd like to think, on smaller scales, too. Case in point: Gamepires, creator of open-world survival game Scum , which announced last week that it's putting people out of work. The bad news came via an unattributed message posted on X : "A difficult decision has been made to reduce the size of the Gamepires team, which means saying goodbye to colleagues who've helped shape Scum and the studio. This step is necessary to help Gamepires adapt to challenging market conditions and long-term sustainability." (Image credit: Gamepires) It's all very bloodless and generic—the sort of statement that could've come from just about any game studio making layoffs over the past six months or so. What makes this particular case feel so egregious, though, is that Gamepires was acquired by Splash Damage Group , in a deal backed by Emona Capital, just eight months ago. And that acquisition was made just three months after Splash Damage made major layoffs of it…

title: 'We probably sold millions of boards because of that game, and it was magnificent': 3dfx cofounder gives Quake a 'great deal of credit for our overall success'
summary: It's now been 30 years since the first Voodoo card.
body: If you care about retro PC gaming hardware, there's a good chance you've heard of the now-defunct 3dfx. And if you know 3dfx, there's an even better chance you've heard of the 3dfx Voodoo graphics card. Well, according to one of its founders, its success is owed at least in part to the legendary shooter Quake. Ross Smith recently spoke to our friends at Club386 in celebration of the first 3dfx Voodoo turning 30 years old, and he talks about the 'Quake effect'. Effectively, though Quake launched in June 1996, it didn't get GLQuake, which allowed for 3D hardware acceleration, until the start of 1997. John Carmack reportedly reached out to 3dfx, which then worked on an API called MiniGL that could run the game. In its implementation, 3dfx cards could then run the game at a better resolution in greater detail with a wider range of colours. Smith says, "I would certainly give id, John, and Quake a great deal of credit for our overall success—we probably sold millions of boards because of that game, and it was magnificent. That’s the last game I’ve gone all the way to the end on, and I was exhausted after doing that. It was well crafted, beautiful, dark." It makes sense why developers w…

title: Ex-BioWare boss and Mass Effect director Casey Hudson says he'll 'forever be grateful' for his time at the studio: 'Its legacy will live on'
summary: The former KotOR director's new studio is working on its own Star Wars entry in the Old Republic era.
body: Yesterday, EA announced that it's closing BioWare , the studio behind beloved RPG franchises like the original Baldur's Gate games, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age. Alongside BioWare's closure—and the cancelling of its next Mass Effect project—EA is reportedly laying off around 400 people in an effort to "align talent and investment" in the wake of its record-breaking private equity buyout . While recent years have brought no shortage of high profile studio closings and game cancellations, the news of BioWare's shuttering has prompted an outpouring of sympathies and frustrations from the fans, fellow developers, and former studio staff. Among those mourners is former BioWare game director and ex-general manager Casey Hudson, who reacted to the news on X to say that BioWare's influence will continue even if the studio itself doesn't. This is sad news on multiple fronts - for those of us who worked there, for our friends and colleagues at BioWare who are impacted, and for fans who were looking forward to the next Mass Effect adventure. title: EA has reportedly put DICE and Respawn to work on a new Star Wars: Battlefront game
summary: It will unlock growth, which I'm pretty excited about.
body: In spite of a bloodletting that saw the end of BioWare —a lion in winter, sure, but still a studio with a rich legacy—and around 400 employees laid off, EA seemingly still has videogame irons in the fire. Per a report from Variety , the corporation is working on a new Battlefront game, said to be in the hands of Respawn and DICE. This is not officially confirmed, of course. In its gore-flecked letter to staff and rubber-neckers in the wake of yesterday's BioWare news, EA only said that its future involved "bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project." This, it boasted, would allow it to "balance our resources, and leverage the technology to deliver a shooter portfolio that unlocks growth." Which certainly gets me excited about things to come. Nevertheless, multiple sources tell Variety that the "future project" is, indeed, a third Battlefront. Which is probably a good idea, in all fairness. title: Only $70 separates RTX 5050, RTX 5060, and RTX 5060 Ti AND the RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB is now the same price as the RTX 5070 in what I can only describe as pure carnage
summary: It's not pretty out there, especially for the RTX 50 series.
body: We prattle on about GPU prices so much nowadays that even we're getting sick of it. Yet for as long as the memory crisis rages on and prices keep rising, we'll keep bringing it up. We'll also keep trying to spot the best prices for graphics cards , which is exactly how I spotted these specific pricing horrors. The RTX 5050, RTX 5060, and RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB are now only separated by a mere $70. That's not between each card—the jump from an RTX 5050 to an RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB is just $70, down from nearly double that at their intended MSRPs. 'What's the big deal, then?' I hear you ask. 'Surely that means less cash for a better card?' It is a big deal, and no, it doesn't. This is due to dreadful circumstances: the cheapest RTX 5050 that I could find is this one currently $400 at Best Buy . It's not only far in excess of the MSRP—which should be a mere $249—but it's actually in excess of the MSRP of the RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB at $379. The cheapest RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB I could find is $470 , and the cheapest RTX 5060 is $420 . title: Game industry legend Warren Spector blows up over BioWare's closure: 'it's utter bulls**t'
summary: The recently retired producer of System Shock, Ultima Underworld, Deus Ex, and so many more wants to know why "the folks in suits" aren't losing their jobs.
body: Immersive sim legend Warren Spector shared some thoughts on yesterday's closure of BioWare, and they're uncharacteristically spicy—so much so that he led into them with a warning for sensitive readers. "I try very hard not to curse at any time but especially in public. Unfortunately for my vocabulary and the delicate sensibilities of some who read this I can’t control myself. Hell, I don’t want to control myself," Spector wrote in a brief message on LinkedIn . "BioWare is more than just another studio. For decades it's played a central role in the history of our medium. They, for many years, as effectively as any studio, married art and commerce. Their work changed things." And then, the cursing, and the warning that sensitive readers should cover their eyes while Warren gives 'em both barrels: "This is such bad news, such a devastating historic event all I can say is that it’s utter bullshit. Anyone who participated in this travesty should be ashamed." It is perhaps not the eruption of ear-scalding profanity you were expecting (or hoping for), but the truth is that Spector has been a studiously even-tempered professional throughout his career. title: How to clear a compound in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
summary: Complete the No One Left order.
body: There are some easy open compounds in Daesong Ridge in the south (Image credit: Infinity Ward) Clearing a compound is one of the early orders you'll have to complete when you arrive in Modern Warfare 4 's DMZ mode, and it requires you to assault a mini enemy stronghold. Compounds are marked with the little tent and flag symbols on the map, though they vary in difficulty, and some of them require keys to open. If you're looking for an easy one to complete, I recommend the two in Daesong Ridge in the south of the map. These army camps are open, so they're easy to access, and they don't have too many enemies. To clear a compound you need to: Kill every enemy in the compound—your current progress is represented by the percentage bar on the left, though it counts up instead of down. When you kill the last enemy in the stronghold, make sure to pick up the Medical Extraction Intel they drop and extract it to complete the order. title: The iconic Windows fish screensaver was inspired by a dentist's office, which makes a lot of sense when you think about it
summary: Top ten screensaver?
body: If you've ever been to a dentist's office, there's a good chance you might associate them with little aquariums. Well, it turns out that link is also how we got the classic After Dark Fish screensaver that PC users enjoyed in the early '90s. That's according to Ed Fries, co-founder of After Dark and former vice president of Game Publishing at Microsoft, who spoke to Jesse Petrilla about it recently. Reportedly, an artist approached Fries as she was working on a scene set in a dentist's office, and "she wanted to have an aquarium in it because there's always an aquarium in a dentist's office." "And she said, is there any way I could have a little part of the screen and have fish move in it?" Fries supposedly told them, "I'm a video game programmer. I can make fish move on the screen. Give me the fish, and I'll make them move." Fries made a looping animation for them, then went back to the artist to ask for some bigger fish characters they could use for "this crazy idea" they had. With the new larger fishes in hand, Fries then stayed late at the office and turned his entire screen into one big aquarium. title: Mass Effect's Amazon series is reportedly continuing after BioWare shutdown, which'll make an uncomfortable gravestone for the studio's work
summary: Here lies BioWare's sci-fi opera, you can tell because we put 'Mass Effect' on the gravestone.
body: BioWare has shut down , and while that doesn't inherently mean we won't be seeing more Mass Effect—EA owns the rights to that IP—the next Mass Effect game's been cancelled, and I certainly wouldn't hold my breath for EA to make anything that isn't sports, Sims, or shooter related in the near future. According to sources who spoke to IGN , however, the TV series , which has been in the works at Prime Video since 2024, will still go ahead. It'll be set after the original trilogy, so it won't be quite so awkward as seeing Commander Shepherd making winks and nods to a series of games built by a slowly-dismantled studio, but still. There's something deeply bittersweet about a videogame series arriving after the studio responsible for its creation has gone out of business. And perhaps reflective of how EA has treated BioWare itself—grabbing a studio known for making some of the best RPGs ever—and chipping away at it. Coasting on the good will from a studio it had precious little interest in managing and rarely gave a fair shot at doing what it was actually good at. I mean, just look at Anthem. I could point to any number of developer tell-alls that might suggest EA didn't know what to d…

title: Star Wars: The Old Republic lead writer calls out BioWare for snubbing the MMO
summary: The long-running MMO didn't get a mention when BioWare announced it was closing.
body: Yesterday was a pretty bleak day for the videogame industry, as BioWare announced the end of its more than 30-year run . It's closing down and development on the next Mass Effect has ceased. For Star Wars: The Old Republic lead writer Caitlin Sullivan Kelly, however, the announcement was upsetting for an additional reason: SWTOR was snubbed. In BioWare's post, shared on social media, the studio listed Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect and Anthem. But not the MMO that's been running for nearly 15 years. Quoting the announcement, Kelly said, "No mention of the game that's been going for almost 15 years, that supported the studio and all of its projects with income and manpower and time (sometimes to our own detriment). Heartbreaking." title: How to get electronic sensors in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
summary: One of two materials you'll need to expand your stash.
body: You can find electronic sensors lying around in buildings, but particularly apartments Infinity Ward And in certain containers Infinity Ward You can also search PCs for them Infinity Ward I got all ten of mine in Hanrim Village in the north, but any packed area of buildings should work Infinity Ward You'll need electronic sensors in Modern Warfare 4 's DMZ mode to upgrade your starting stash, which quickly runs out of space after the first couple of matches. Unlike rigid synthetics, the other material you need, you likely won't find enough electronic sensors without looking in the right place. The best places to get electronic sensors are: Inside buildings, but particularly apartments and apartment blocks. I found quite a few as loose items or inside bags. Inside computers. If you spot a computer, open it up and take a look. title: Can you identify the horror game by its horrors?
summary: Put a name to the nightmare.
body: You'd think someone who still screams at the sight of the Tomb Raider T-Rex wouldn't be so into horror games, but I can't help myself; I love 'em. I'm always down for a good inhuman gurgle or unnatural skitter across the floor. Creature with too many eyeballs? Sign me up. Inordinate number of hands? I'm on my way. More quizzes! (Image credit: Future) Want to keep testing your knowledge of gaming trivia? We've got loads more PC Gamer quizzes , on everything from healthbars to weird currencies to absurd patch notes. That enthusiasm for terror is why I have the nervous system of a small woodland creature, but also why I can rattle off a list of favorite ghosts and ghouls like they're important historical figures. It's the perfect special interest for a PC Gamer quiz, so today I'm asking: How many horror games can you identify from a screenshot of one of their resident monstrosities? You've got 12 minutes to face your fears and name as many games as you can from a glimpse of their ghosts, ghouls, and other unspeakable horrors.
